title: Decouple route evaluation and implement capacity-aware fallback orchestrator
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Refactor the smart routing layer by separating policy evaluation from execution and adding a capacity-aware fallback orchestrator. Current policy engine mixes evaluation, capacity checks, and region selection which makes incremental fixes risky and leads to surprising fallbacks under load. This ticket breaks the logic into three components: (1) pure policy evaluator (stateless rules + weights), (2) capacity/cost inspector (reads real-time capacity metrics and quotas), and (3) fallback orchestrator that composes decisions and executes safe fallbacks with throttling and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Route decisions are produced by the policy evaluator with no side effects; 2) Capacity inspector returns consistent capacity states for all regions/pools and is covered by unit tests and a synthetic load harness; 3) Fallback orchestrator performs fallbacks deterministically and logs an auditable decision trace; 4) End-to-end canary against 5% of traffic shows no SLO regressions (latency P50/P95 within 5% of baseline); 5) Rollback path validated in staging and rollback runbook added to the console release notes.
decision_notes: Chose to keep a lightweight policy DSL (existing JSON rules) rather than adopt a full policy language to minimize dev churn and preserve current expressivity.
Implemented capacity inspector as a pluggable adapter so Dedicated and Private deployments can provide their own telemetry source.
Fallback orchestrator will prefer capacity-aware downgraded model variants over cross-region failover when cost delta < configured threshold.
Avoided a single monolithic state machine; opted for a small composable pipeline to ease testing and future A/B routing experiments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (infra & tests): Add capacity inspector interface + synthetic metrics collector (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (eval refactor): Extract policy evaluator into its own package with unit and property tests (1 week).
Phase 3 (orchestrator): Implement fallback orchestrator & decision tracing + integrate with existing router (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (canary): Deploy to staging then 5% production canary, monitor cost/latency and rollback path (1 week).
Phase 5 (cleanup): Remove deprecated code paths, update runbooks and console docs (3 days).
risks: Regression in tail latency if batching/kv cache interactions are missed during refactor.
Incorrect capacity signals from Dedicated customers could cause excessive fallbacks; mitigated by adapter sandboxing and fail-open default.
Complexity of fallback policies may cause oscillation; will add backoff and cooldown windows in orchestrator.
benchmarks: Baseline (prod sampling): mean routing decision time = 2.8ms, P95 9.6ms.
Goal: evaluator + inspector combined decision time < 3.5ms and P95 < 12ms under typical load.
Staging synthetic: extracted evaluator reduced end-to-end router CPU by ~12% in the 95th percentile under 5000 qps load.
